question: Which of the following crops takes almost a year to grow?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sugarcane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sugarcane is a tropical and subtropical crop, grown in a warm climate with abundant water supply.
 
• The crop cycle for sugarcane varies from 10 to 18 months, depending on the variety and growing conditions.
 
• In India, sugarcane planting typically begins in February to April and harvesting starts from November to March of the following year.
 
• This crop requires a long growing period to accumulate high sugar content in the stalks, making it a year-long cultivation.
 
• Sugarcane is primarily grown in states like Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Andhra Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ratoon Cropping:** Sugarcane can be ratooned, meaning the regrowth from the stubbles of the harvested crop can be used for the next planting.
 
• **Water Requirements:** The crop requires about 1500-2500 mm of water throughout its growing period, which is why irrigation plays a crucial role in sugarcane farming.
 
• **Soil Type:** Sugarcane thrives in well-drained loamy soil with a pH range of 6.5 to 7.5, though it can grow in a variety of soils.
 
• **Economic Importance:** Sugarcane is a major source of sugar and ethanol production, contributing significantly to the agricultural economy in many countries.
 
• **By-products:** Bagasse, a by-product of sugarcane, is used in the production of paper, and as a biofuel for electricity generation in sugar mills.
